title: Uniform Normal Calibration of Three-Split Ridge Slope Estimators under Non-Gaussian Designs
banked_reason: D0.5 math and decision PASS; five sources cited-verified-attested; authoritative graded subfield below field floor, projected score6.5<7.4 and salvageablefalse. Independent main validity confirms sound but estimator-specific impact ceiling; standing operator bank downgraded stop.
gap_reasons: The delivered contribution is calibration of one prescribed three-split statistic under known residual normalization and independent design coordinates, rather than a general partially linear inference framework.

The penalty-optimization theorem establishes objective-value attainment, not the variance, normality, or coverage of the selected statistic; the framing explicitly respects that boundary and contains no stale claim of selected-penalty coverage.

The projected score is constrained by the restricted estimator and noise model, the limited operational content of variance-value tuning, and the absence of reproducible finite-sample comparisons establishing the practical calibration benefit.

[D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6.5 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
proof_attempt_summary: Two discovery proof rounds discharged the uniform non-Gaussian fitted-product law, localization-sensitive total variance, original-record studentization and compact-penalty variance-objective optimization for the prescribed three-split statistic. Both D0.5 panel referees passed; all five cited sources were directly verified, and the iid quadratic-form source scope was repaired with all 12 dependent proofs independently revalidated. The cold score ceiling 6.5 below the field floor 7.4 ended the run at subfield: selected-penalty inference and finite-sample comparisons remain outside the delivered package, and no F/Lean certification was attempted.
tldr: The prescribed three-split ridge statistic has a uniform normal law for the normalized causal slope under iid non-Gaussian coordinates with bounded ninth moments, arbitrary coefficient localization, and aspect ratios through one. Its evaluated total variance includes both training fits, their product, held-out variation, and the correction \(9\kappa r_1^2r_2^2L\). Original-record moments give a total positive variance estimate and fixed-public-penalty Wald coverage. On a public compact positive penalty rectangle, the variance approximation and feasible objective are uniformly consistent, so approximate feasible minimizers attain the oracle variance value. This optimization guarantee does not assert coverage after penalty selection.
gap: The source leaves non-Gaussian variance calibration beyond its Gaussian variance theorem. Published directional spectral theory does not directly settle the pinned statistic with changing laws, random fitted directions, and original-record studentization.
fill: An exact training/evaluation decomposition, a uniform negative-resolvent fluctuation extension, and coordinate moment recovery support the requested total variance and uniform Wald law. The actual variance coefficients and feasible construction are derived outputs.
